findings.title: Mutable import-time default for `queued` timestamp
findings.body: In src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py line 18, `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once at import time. Every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` shares the same timestamp. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Consequence is stale/incorrect `queued` metadata on all sources and broken tests that assume freshness.

findings.title: AssignmentSource.to_dict emits non-JSON datetime into Celery task
findings.body: AssignmentSource.to_dict() in src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py uses dataclasses.asdict, which leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object. src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py then puts that dict into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... assignment_source_dict ...})`. Celery kwargs must be JSON-serializable, so enqueue will raise a serialization error and outbound assignee sync will never run. Even if serialized by another serializer, `from_dict` does not parse an ISO string back to datetime, so the round-trip is broken and a malformed dict returns None and fails open to re-syncing.
